items.name: Obsidian Smoke Globe
items.short_description: Hand-blown borosilicate globe with volcanic ash inclusions on an oxidized copper tripod.
items.long_description: Each globe is blown over three sessions at a 1,200°C furnace, volcanic ash and black iron oxide suspended in the gather before the final seal. No two internal smoke patterns are identical — the inclusions drift and reorient as the glass cools, leaving a permanent record of the exact atmospheric conditions in the studio that day. The tripod is fabricated from 3mm copper rod, hand-bent and oxidized with liver of sulfur to a deep verdigris-black. Edition of three.
items.care: Dust with microfiber. Avoid prolonged direct sunlight — the internal glass acts as a lens and can concentrate heat.

items.name: Damascus-Fold Letter Opener
items.short_description: 200-layer hand-forged damascus blade with ebonized white oak handle and a hand-turned copper collar.
items.long_description: Folded and drawn out by hand from a billet of 1084 and 15N20 high-carbon steel. Two hundred layers. The pattern emerges from the etch — unpredictable, unrepeatable. The blade is sharpened because a dull thing in a good hand is an insult to the hand. Handle scales of ebonized white oak, fitted with a hand-turned copper collar finished to match the blade's warm highlights. A thing made to be passed down.
items.care: Oil blade lightly with camellia oil monthly. Keep dry. The etch patina deepens with handling — this is correct.

items.name: Lost-Wax Bronze Celestial Weight
items.short_description: Cast in solid silicon bronze via lost-wax process. Hand-engraved with the northern celestial hemisphere from a 17th-century atlas.
items.long_description: The star map is taken directly from a 17th-century celestial atlas, redrawn by hand and transferred to a wax form for investment casting. Silicon bronze — chosen for its warm golden tone — was poured at 1,080°C. The casting was hand-chased for twelve hours to restore fine detail. Patinated in three layers: potassium sulfide for depth, ferric nitrate for warmth, and a final carnauba wax seal. Two exist. They will not be made again.
items.care: The patina is fully stable. Handling will burnish contact points over time — this is the intended finish evolution.

items.name: Hammered Copper Still Vessel
items.short_description: Ornamental copper vessel in the form of a small alchemical still. Hand hammer-raised from 18-gauge sheet. Tin-lined interior.
items.long_description: Modeled after the cucurbit-and-alembic configuration used in 16th-century distillation practice — this is not a functional still. It is an argument that the most important laboratory was always the room you live in. Fabricated from 18-gauge copper sheet, hammer-raised over hardwood stakes. The surface carries 4,000 individual hammer strikes, each visible as a facet catching light. The interior is hand-tinned for display of dry botanicals or as a vessel for single malt. Three made.
items.care: Allow the patina to develop naturally. A living copper surface is part of the object's biography. Interior tin: rinse with cool water only.

items.name: MOVA Globe — Antique Earth Edition
items.short_description: Self-rotating globe driven by ambient light and Earth's magnetic field. No batteries. No maintenance. Ever.
items.long_description: The MOVA Globe rotates continuously using only ambient light — photovoltaic cells hidden behind the map surface convert indoor light levels into enough current to spin the globe against the Earth's magnetic field. The Antique Earth edition uses a sepia-toned cartographic print derived from 19th-century Rand McNally plates, with hand-applied relief shading. The outer acrylic sphere is filled with a refractive fluid that optically enlarges the rotating globe within and protects it from dust. One rotation every 72 seconds. It will outlast the room.
items.care: No maintenance required. Ensure moderate ambient light. The refractive fluid is factory-sealed for life.

items.name: Meridian Perpetual Calendar
items.short_description: Three independently rotating knurled brass dials for day, date, and month. Engraved numerals — not printed.
items.long_description: Three knurled brass dials, each independently set by hand. The day dial has 7 positions, the date dial 31, the month dial 12. The numerals and text are engraved, not printed — they will still be legible in a hundred years. The base is solid brass, sand-cast and hand-finished to an aged patina using liver-of-sulfur treatment. The whole assembly weighs 340 grams. There is no digital equivalent of the small decision to turn the date dial forward each morning.
items.care: Tarnish can be reversed with a light application of brass polish. The patina is a choice, not a flaw.

items.name: Vachetta Leather Desk Pad
items.short_description: Full-surface pad in unfinished vachetta leather. Hand saddle-stitched. Darkens beautifully with use.
items.long_description: Vachetta is the same leather used on the handles of classic French luggage — vegetable-tanned, unfinished, undyed. It sells pale and chalky and becomes, through use and light, a deep caramel unique to the person using it. The coffee ring, the pen mark, the oil of a hand rested — these are the patina. Sized for a full monitor and keyboard setup. The underside has a natural suede finish that grips without adhesive. Edges are folded and saddle-stitched by hand with waxed linen thread.
items.care: Apply a light coat of neatsfoot oil every 6–12 months. It will age — that aging is the object becoming yours.

items.name: Aerospace Brass Fidget Spinner
items.short_description: Precision-machined from solid C360 brass. ABEC-9 ceramic hybrid bearing. 4-minute rated spin time. 148g.
items.long_description: This began as a 6-inch round of C360 free-machining brass. Turned on a CNC lathe to ±0.005mm tolerance, then hand-polished through 800, 1200, and 2000 grit before a final rouge finish. The three lobes are balanced to within 0.1 grams of each other — any looser and you feel it in the spin. The center bearing is an ABEC-9 ceramic hybrid: steel races, silicon nitride balls, no lubrication needed. Four-minute rated spin time under a single moderate flick. Weight is the point: 148 grams in your palm is not a toy.
items.care: Polish with microfiber to maintain mirror finish. Bearing is sealed and maintenance-free.

items.name: Tsuru Cast-Iron Incense Set
items.short_description: Set of three Nambu-style cast-iron crane figures at staggered heights. Holds stick or cone incense.
items.long_description: The tsuru (鶴) is a crane, and in Japan it carries the weight of a thousand-year wish. These three figures are cast in traditional Nambu-style iron from a sand mold and hand-finished with a natural lacquer seal that resists rust. Each crane stands at a slightly different height; together they form a composition. A small notch at the beak holds stick incense; the base collar catches ash from cone incense. The iron darkens further with use and heat, becoming blacker and more itself.
items.care: Avoid prolonged water contact. Wipe dry after use. Do not use soap — it strips the seasoning.

items.name: Highland Whisky Stones + Leather Pouch
items.short_description: Eight tumbled Connemara marble stones from the west of Ireland, with hand-stitched full-grain leather drawstring pouch.
items.long_description: These are not soapstone. Soapstone scratches, breaks, and doesn't hold temperature. These are tumbled Connemara marble from the west of Ireland — the green-veined stone that was beneath the bogs before the bogs existed. Marble conducts cold better than soapstone and looks markedly better in a glass. Each stone tumbled smooth with no sharp edges. Eight stones fit two glasses. The pouch is hand-stitched full-grain leather with a waxed linen drawstring. It will outlive the stones by decades.
items.care: Rinse stones and air-dry before returning to pouch. Do not freeze inside the leather pouch.

items.name: Coptic-Stitch Hand-Bound Journal
items.short_description: Hand-sewn in the Coptic tradition. Lies completely flat when open. 320 pages of 120gsm Tomoe River paper.
items.long_description: The Coptic stitch — used by Egyptian bookbinders since the 4th century — produces a book that opens completely flat, every page, without cracking the spine, because there is no spine. The spine is open, the signatures visible, the thread pattern itself part of the aesthetic. Covers are 3mm bookbinder's board wrapped in natural undyed kozo paper. Pages are 120gsm Tomoe River, the preferred paper for fountain pen users for its near-zero bleed on even the wettest nibs. 320 pages, numbered in a small corner serif. Five exist.
items.care: Keep dry. The kozo cover can be spot-cleaned with a barely damp cloth and air-dried flat.

items.name: Gravity Paradox Sphere
items.short_description: Hand-turned black walnut sphere that disassembles into 12 interlocking pieces. No glue, no screws, no magnets. Gravity holds it.
items.long_description: Twelve pieces of American black walnut, turned on a lathe and fitted to within 0.1mm tolerance. The assembly is self-locking under gravity — it holds itself without glue, screws, or magnets. Disassembly requires a specific sequence of moves in a specific order. Then it falls apart in your hands. Reassembly is about finding the logic embedded in the wood. The surface is finished with a single coat of Danish oil, which enhances the walnut grain without filling it. No two are identical — the grain makes them different objects.
items.care: Keep dry. Danish oil can be refreshed annually with a light wipe. Do not force pieces.

items.name: Maritime Brass Compass Weight
items.short_description: Functional sand-cast brass compass on a weighted base. 32-point hand-engraved rose. 19th-century surveying instrument aesthetic.
items.long_description: A working compass in solid brass — not the kind where the needle sticks. The mechanism is a liquid-filled gimbal-mounted needle that settles to magnetic north with a satisfying stillness. The rose is hand-engraved with 32 cardinal and intercardinal points in the traditional manner, with the fleur-de-lis marking north as it has for six centuries. The base is sand-cast brass, aged to match the instrument. It weighs enough to stay where you put it. This is a navigational instrument that has nowhere left to navigate. Its new job is to remind you that north still exists.
items.care: Keep away from strong magnets and speaker systems. Brass polish annually if desired.
